clue.text: Struggle with part of debrief for troops

indicators.note: 'part of' says the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

blocks.note: the letters straddle the end of the first word, the second word and the start of the third

explanation.surface: An army debriefing turns out to be a struggle for the soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: An effort is a strenuous attempt, which is what a struggle is.

clue.text: Suspend former Conservative over drug dealing

blocks.note: to suspend something is to hang it
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A call to suspend an ex-Tory politician caught up in drug dealing.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' places the former Conservative above the word for suspend, which then sits on the drug.
explanation.definitionFit: Exchange is trading or swapping goods, the same commercial sense as dealing.

clue.text: Fellow's quiet during marine trip with angler

indicators.note: to trip is to stumble, so the word before it falls into a new order
something happening during something else lies within it

blocks.note: F is the abbreviation for fellow
taken as written, to be rearranged
the hushing sound asking for quiet

explanation.surface: A man keeps quiet while out on a sea trip with someone who fishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Marine trip' reads as a boat outing, but trip is the anagram signal acting on marine alone.
explanation.definitionFit: An angler catches fish with rod and line, so is a fisherman.

clue.text: Cricketer has shirt underneath jumper

blocks.note: a roo, short for kangaroo, is a famous jumper

explanation.surface: A cricketer wears a shirt under his sweater.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumper' is British for a sweater, which fits the cricket picture, but here it is a kangaroo; 'underneath' puts the shirt below it in this down answer. Joe Root is an England batsman.
explanation.definitionFit: Joe Root is a celebrated England Test cricketer, so the answer is an example of a cricketer.

clue.text: Increases range of drink to include cold beers

indicators.note: to include something is to take it inside, so the drink word wraps round what follows

blocks.note: C for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A bar extends its drinks list by stocking chilled beers.
explanation.definitionFit: To scale something up is to increase its size or extent, widening its range.

clue.text: Defeat criminal with detailed question

indicators.note: de-tailed means with its tail cut off, so the last letter goes

explanation.surface: A criminal is beaten by a searching, detailed question in the dock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Detailed' looks like it means thorough, but it means lose the tail.
explanation.definitionFit: To conquer an opponent is to overcome or defeat them.

clue.text: Shaggy wanted to cover first of hits broadcast

indicators.note: 'first of' keeps only the opening letter of the next word
covering something means going round it, so one word wraps the others

blocks.note: to air a programme is to broadcast it

explanation.surface: Someone wanted a cover version of their hit songs on the radio.
explanation.definitionFit: Shaggy hair is long and unkempt, so a shaggy creature is long-haired.

clue.text: Parody of spouse is useless and cruel

indicators.note: read as use-less, the spouse word is left without its use
cruel treatment mangles the letters into a different order

blocks.note: taken as written, to be cut down

explanation.surface: A send-up of a husband or wife as a useless, cruel partner.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'useless' as use-less: the letters U, S, E come out of the partner word. 'Of' looks like the link after the definition but is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A spoof is a humorous imitation, the same as a parody.

clue.text: Dad's essentially fattening everyone up with Spanish food!

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its core, so the central letter is kept
in a down answer, going up means reading from bottom to top

explanation.surface: Dad's cooking is basically fattening everyone up with Spanish dishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dad's essentially' suggests the middle of dad, but the selector works on the following word.
explanation.definitionFit: Paella is a Valencian rice dish, a classic Spanish food.

clue.text: Write sadly about husband's decline

indicators.note: something done sadly is done badly, so the letters come out wrong
about means around, so the jumbled word goes round the next piece

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A spouse writes sadly about her husband's failing health.
explanation.definitionFit: To wither is to shrivel and fade, i.e. to decline in vigour.

clue.text: Carer gets a discount applied

indicators.note: letters applied or put to work are reworked into a new arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A care worker receives a staff discount on purchases.
explanation.definitionFit: A custodian is a guardian or keeper, someone who takes care of something.

clue.text: Slipknot soon to tour Spain

indicators.note: a tour goes round and comes back, so the word is read from the other end

blocks.note: E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: The metal band Slipknot will soon go on tour in Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: Slipknot is a US heavy metal band, which is why 'tour' sounds natural.
explanation.definitionFit: A noose is a loop with a running knot that tightens when pulled, a slipknot.

clue.text: A new setter put in last word…

indicators.note: putting something in places it inside the other pieces

blocks.note: the setter refers to themself as me

explanation.surface: A new compiler has inserted the final word of the puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: Amen is said at the close of a prayer, literally the last word.

clue.text: …but with fault corrected, no 'a' needed for 'kind'

indicators.note: saying a letter is not needed removes it from the word in question
correcting puts things in a different order

blocks.note: taken as written, to be cut and rearranged

explanation.surface: Continuing the setter's story: the error is fixed, and no article is needed.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this to the previous clue's surface only. FAULT without its A is FULT, then rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone thoughtful is considerate of others, which is to be kind.

clue.text: Perhaps Taylor Swift's heartily becoming Queen of England!

indicators.note: taking something heartily, from the heart, keeps only the central letter

blocks.note: Elizabeth Taylor was the film star; 'perhaps' marks Taylor as one example of a surname that fits
the central letter of the surname

explanation.surface: A gushing headline crowns the pop star Taylor Swift as England's queen.
explanation.walkthrough: Taylor and Swift want to stay together as the singer; the setter separates them, taking Elizabeth Taylor and the heart of swift.
explanation.definitionFit: Elizabeth I reigned as monarch of England from 1558 to 1603.

clue.text: Better to have old King taking stroll inside

indicators.note: the king takes the walk into himself, so it sits within his letters
inside confirms the walk goes within the royal letters

blocks.note: Georgius Rex, the cipher of the Georges

explanation.surface: It would be better for the former monarch to take a gentle walk inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Better' reads as an adjective, but it is one who bets.
explanation.definitionFit: A better is someone who places bets, i.e. a gambler.

clue.text: Suggested taking time-out from angry tirades

indicators.note: taking something out of a word removes those letters
angry outbursts throw the letters into disorder

explanation.surface: Someone recommended a cooling-off break from furious rants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Time-out' is a hyphenated phrase in the surface; cryptically it is time, removed.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise an issue is to bring it up or put it forward, so raised means suggested.

clue.text: Toleration is aim you said organised church is supporting

indicators.note: said means as spoken, so we want a letter that sounds like the word

blocks.note: the letter U sounds like you
to run an event is to organise it

explanation.surface: Someone claims that organised religion's aim is to support tolerance.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'is supporting' puts the church at the bottom, holding up the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Endurance is the ability to put up with hardship, a form of toleration.

clue.text: Harbour yard disregarded current issue with shed

indicators.note: a letter that is disregarded is ignored and left out

blocks.note: a jetty is a landing stage in a harbour
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A harbourside yard ignored a problem with its boathouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shed' looks like a building but is a verb, to cast off.
explanation.definitionFit: To jettison is to throw away or cast off, which is to shed.

clue.text: Always oversleep after stag night starts stylish

indicators.note: starts are opening letters, so each of the two words gives only its first
the always word is placed over the sleep word, covering it on both sides

blocks.note: the first letter of each word
ay, or aye, is an old word for always
split as over plus sleep; sleep is the cartoon snoozing symbol, and over is the wrapping signal

explanation.surface: After a stag party you always sleep in, but you look stylish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oversleep' is one word in the surface; the setter splits off 'over' to wrap AY around the snoring letters. A stag night is a groom's pre-wedding party.
explanation.definitionFit: Snazzy is informal for smart and eye-catching, i.e. stylish.

clue.text: In the past you sorted out a tour for career break

indicators.note: sorting things out rearranges them

blocks.note: ye is the old form of you
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: You once organised a world trip as a break from work.
explanation.definitionFit: A year out is a year spent away from study or work, a sabbatical-style break.

clue.text: Persuade wife to attend to fringes on lampshade

indicators.note: fringes are edges, so only the outermost letters are kept

blocks.note: to heed is to pay attention to

explanation.surface: A husband coaxes his wife into sorting out the tassels on a lampshade.
explanation.definitionFit: To wheedle is to coax or win someone over with flattery, i.e. to persuade.

clue.text: Maybe every Sunday eke out money in extremes of worry

definitions.note: an example of something weekly; the adverb fits as 'happening weekly'

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two ends
out suggests the letters are knocked out of their order
in places the preceding pieces inside the outer pair of letters

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
L for pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: Someone stretches their cash each Sunday, always on the edge of worry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eke out money' reads as a single idiom, but out is the anagram signal working on eke.
explanation.definitionFit: Something happening every Sunday recurs once a week, so it is an example of weekly.

clue.text: Child's hidden in toilets, upset with swimming group

indicators.note: in a down answer, upset means turned upside down, so read bottom to top
being hidden in something means sitting inside it

explanation.surface: A distressed child is hiding in the toilets to avoid swimming lessons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hidden in' tempts a hidden-word search; it is a container here.
explanation.definitionFit: A school is a large group of fish swimming together, like a shoal.

clue.text: Famous sweetheart's wearing bracelet shimmering with diamonds

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its central letter
something worn sits inside what wears it
a shimmer makes things move and waver, so the letters shift

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
the heart of sweet, its central letter
D for diamonds, the card suit

explanation.surface: A famous person's partner is wearing a glittering diamond bracelet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweetheart' looks like a lover; split it as sweet-heart for its middle letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A celebrated person is renowned and widely acclaimed, i.e. famous.

clue.text: Gauchos salsa with some spinning rope

indicators.note: some of the words means only part of their letters is used
spinning turns the run of letters round to face the other way

blocks.note: the letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: South American cowboys dance the salsa while twirling a rope.
explanation.walkthrough: Gauchos are Argentine cowboys, who really do use such ropes.
explanation.definitionFit: A lasso is a rope with a running noose used to catch cattle.

clue.text: Brood about stopping newspaper

indicators.note: something stopping a gap is plugged inside it

blocks.note: the Financial Times, this very paper

explanation.surface: Someone sulks over the paper being shut down.
explanation.definitionFit: To fret is to worry anxiously, much as one broods over a problem.

clue.text: Look beneath odd hoax for a sign of saintliness

indicators.note: odd letters are those in positions one, three and so on

explanation.surface: A strange trick hunts for proof of a saint's holiness.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'beneath' puts the look word below the other piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A halo is the ring of light painted around a saint's head to signify holiness.

clue.text: Old TV name's arrested for assault

indicators.note: something arrested is held, caught inside its captor

explanation.surface: A veteran television personality has been arrested for assault.
explanation.definitionFit: An onset is an attack or onslaught, the old sense of an assault.

clue.text: Suffering lots, I struggle to comprehend artistic medium

definitions.note: singular here, while the answer is plural; paints collectively are the medium

indicators.note: a struggle throws things about, so the letters land in a new order
to comprehend is literally to take in, so the jumble holds the other piece

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An artist suffers a great deal, struggling to understand the medium.
explanation.definitionFit: Oil paints are pigments in oil, a medium in which artists work.

clue.text: Investigate family drawn into stolen goods ring

indicators.note: being drawn into something pulls it inside

explanation.surface: Police investigate a family caught up in a stolen goods gang.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring' looks like a criminal gang, but it is just the round letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To look into a matter is to examine or investigate it.

clue.text: Elect to veto appalling independent nationalist

indicators.note: something appalling is a mess, so the letters come out wrong

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A choice to block a dreadful independent nationalist candidate.
explanation.definitionFit: To vote someone in is to elect them to office.
